_about: The torches of chapter 4's dark levels, and the wall of light one drops.
Decoded from android_game.bin, ETHCallback_light_off.angelscript, whose fourteen
functions are the whole mechanism: bytes 467198..473086.
entity_roles.json calls the role `torch` and files light_off / light_off.ent under it,
with the note 'an unlit torch that can be switched on ... this is what makes the dark
levels navigable'. That note is right about the importance and wrong about the shape:
what makes those levels navigable is not the LIGHT, it is that lighting a torch takes a
IT IS A TOGGLE, NOT AN UNLOCK, and reading it as an unlock is the trap. Shooting the
unlit torch lights it and drops the wall. Shooting the orbiting flame that appears puts
the torch back out and REBUILDS the wall. A port that built only the first half would
play every level correctly and still be wrong about the mechanism.

_note: ETHCallback_light_off spins its sprite (AddToAngle at 190 units a second) and each
frame calls hasProjectileAround(GetPositionXY(), 24, includeFireballs). That helper is
a bucket walk that accepts an entity named projectile.ent OR - when the flag is set,
and the call site pushes immediate 1 - fireball.ent, inside squaredDistance of
scale(24). So a FIRE DIAMOND'S FIREBALLS WORK THESE SWITCHES TOO, which is the third
place step 27's mechanism turned out to be load-bearing.
Lighting one, in the callback's own order: add light_from_projectile.ent and
light_on_sparkles.ent, set its own `delete` flag, killProjectile (the shot is SPENT -
the same bare DeleteEntity the fire diamond's conversion uses), add portal_death.ent,
playLightOnSound, seekLightWallToDestroy, addFireSignalIfNecessary.
On the NEXT frame the `delete` branch runs: SetAmbientLight(0.1, 0.1, 0.25) - lighter
than darkest's 0.01 but not lit - lightenAllBackgroundEntitities, GenerateLightmaps,
and it deletes itself. So a lit torch is GONE as an entity, not redrawn.
seekLightWallToDestroy is SeekEntity('light_wall.ent') - the FIRST one, and every
level that has one has exactly one - then destroy(wall), then a dashed_door.ent named
`light_wall_ghost` at the wall's position and angle, offset z by -4. The ghost is not
decoration: it is the bookmark addLightWall builds the wall back from.
destroy() only sets a flag. ETHCallback_light_wall then counts elapsedTime: at 800 ms
playLightSwitchSound, and only at 1500 ms playDemolitionSound, wall_destroy.ent,
startEarthquake(20, 0) and DeleteEntity. Until destroyed it fades its alpha UP toward 1.
THE 1500 ms IS LOAD-BEARING, not a flourish. addFireSignalIfNecessary runs immediately
after seekLightWallToDestroy and only spawns a signal when SeekEntity STILL finds a
light_wall.ent - which it does, because the wall is flagged and not yet deleted. Were
the wall taken away on the frame it was flagged, no signal could ever appear and the
toggle would be a one-way unlock.
With one torch and one wall per level there is exactly one signal, and no second torch
can be lit inside the window to ask for another.
The wall is a real solid. In the levels it is a Node2D with a StaticBody2D and a
CollisionPolygon2D about 30 x 126, and it carries metadata/breakable = 1 - so the port
already has it in Demolish::Breakable with a body and a box. Removing it therefore goes
THROUGH Demolish rather than behind its back, as a struck minion goes through
Minions::Take: a body destroyed behind a module that walks its own list every frame is
how that list ends up holding an invalid entity.
ETHCallback_fire_signal stores originalPos on its first frame, then each frame adds to
an `angle` custom datum (incrementAngleCustomData, 300 a second) and puts itself at
originalPos + scale(18) * (-cos(angle), sin(angle)). So it CIRCLES the torch it came
from rather than sitting on it, and the thing the player has to hit is moving.
Hit - the same hasProjectileAround(pos, 24, includeFireballs) - and it reverses the
whole thing: add a fresh light_off.ent at originalPos, add light_off_sparkles.ent,
killProjectile, set `switch` = 1 on the new torch, deleteLightFromProjectile, delete
itself, add portal_death.ent, darkenAllBackgroundEntitities, SetAmbientLight back to
DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT, extinguish_fire.ent, playLightOffSound, GenerateLightmaps, and
addLightWall.
addLightWall seeks the `light_wall_ghost`, adds light_wall_create.ent and a new
light_wall.ent at the ghost's position and angle, sets the new wall's alpha to 0 (the
wall's own callback fades it up), and deletes the ghost.
`switch` = 1 on the recreated torch is what entity_roles.json's note means by 'switch
custom data on the 4 inline ones'. Nothing in the decode READS it; it marks a torch
that was put back out rather than placed. Carried here, acted on by nothing.
What a lit torch sets the level's ambient light to, against darkest's
(0.01, 0.01, 0.01) in art.json. Recorded and applied by NOTHING, for the same reason
art.json's darkest block is: this port has no ambient light and Sprites carries no
colour for it to multiply. The pair of numbers is kept together so that when lighting
exists, both ends of it are already decoded.

_census: 10 torches across 10 levels, exactly ONE each: level21c, level22c, level23c, level24c,
level25c, level26c, level28c, level29c, level30c, level31c. Every one of them is a
`darkest` level, and no level outside that ten places one.
That one-per-level was measured, and a first pass here said three. The three came from
counting grep LINES rather than nodes: a torch is a node header, a metadata/entity_name
line and a child Sprite line. The same trap had already been caught for light_wall - 5
lines, 1 wall - and was walked straight back into for light_off. Counting lines is not
6 light walls across 6 levels, exactly 1 each: level25c, level26c, level28c, level29c,
level30c, level31c. So FOUR of the ten torch levels - level21c to level24c - have NO
wall at all, and there a torch only lights the room and spends a shot. Those four were
already finishable; the other six were not, and that is what this step fixes.
light_wall.ent, dashed_door.ent and fire_signal.ent are in NO role table at all, so
Roles::RoleOf returns empty for them and Roles::IsPorted answers true - they have never
once been reported inert. Nothing would have flagged a level standing behind an
unremovable wall; the suite has to.
_not_built: Every picture and every sound: light_from_projectile.ent, light_on_sparkles.ent,
wall_destroy.ent, the dashed_door ghost's own sprite, playLightOnSound,
when a wall goes, the torch's 190-a-second spin, and the wall's alpha fade.
There is no ambient light in this port to change.
bounceLightEntity, and the `bounce` flag addFireSignalIfNecessary sets on an existing
light_from_projectile.ent. Presentation, and unreachable here besides.
